form.notes: NOT READ. The form and the checklist (http://static.azdeq.gov/ogcc/checklists/form03_checklist.pdf) are on static.azdeq.gov, and one GET of the form came back HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment, enable JavaScript and cookies' page; a filed APD on ogviewer.azdeq.gov answered the same way. Not retried and no other route tried, per the brief. Cells marked form therefore rest on the rule A.A.C. R12-7-104 (read at https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/arizona/Ariz-Admin-Code-SS-R12-7-104): an application on the Commission's form with operator name, address and phone and a description of the proposed well and location; a well and well-site construction plan (R12-7-108 to -118, not read); a surveyor-certified plat with acreage, exact location and ground elevation; an organization report; a performance bond; and a $25.00 per well fee; 30 days for completeness and 30 for review; permit void after 180 days without operations. The data layer's columns show what the agency records per permit.

sources.tested: Found by following the azogcc.az.gov 'View Map' link to an ArcGIS Experience whose config names this layer. Layer ?f=json: HTTP 200, 20 KB, point layer, max 2,000 records, Query only. One query of all rows without geometry: HTTP 200, 1,995,806 bytes, 1,288 rows (not truncated). Counts: Unknown status 856, Abandoned 190, Plugged 95, Shut In 34, Permit Expired 23, Active 20, Permit Extension 19, Producing 14, Planned 12, Permitted 9. Well type: Oil and Gas Exploration 1,070, Helium 73, Geothermal 66, Gas 18, Gas Storage 16, CO2 14. Spud years since 2020: 13, 1, 7, 7, 0, 1 (2020 to 2025). STATUS_DATE runs to 2026-09-12, LAST_EDITED_DATE to 2026-09-24. Permit numbers run to 1324 (2026-07). The layer has no approval or filing date column; CREATED_DATE is filled for 9 rows only (from 2025-09).

grade_reason: A free, reachable ArcGIS layer with one row per permitted or drilled well (permit number, API, operator, county, TRS, lat/long, depth, formation, spud date, status and status date), updated in 2026. It has no approval or filing date: the only dates are spud, end of drilling and the date of the current status, so monthly permit counts are approximate. Volume is small (about 80 permits since 2020, mostly helium in Apache County, plus geothermal in Greenlee).
producer_plan: Query the layer (where=1=1, outFields=*, returnGeometry=false; 1,288 rows, 2 MB, under the 2,000-row limit) once a night or week and keep each snapshot, because the layer is a current-state table. A permit counts as new in the first snapshot where its PERMIT_ID appears (numbers are sequential: 1317 in Sep 2025, 1324 in Jul 2026), and the approval can be dated by the first snapshot with STATUS_WELL = Permitted and the STATUS_DATE then shown. For history before the first snapshot, STATUS_DATE of rows still at Permitted, Permit Extension or Permit Expired is a rough date; SPUD_DATE gives wells spudded by month (New Mexico style). Activity types come from WELL_TYPE and COMMODITY (oil and gas, helium, CO2, geothermal, storage); new drill versus re-entry is not in the layer (NOTES text such as 'reapply for permit AZOGCC:1271' marks a reissue). The exact approval date is in each approval-letter PDF's file name on the per-well page (azogcc.az.gov/<permit>), but those PDFs sit behind a Cloudflare challenge that refused this machine, so they may refuse a GitHub runner too. Expect 0 to 15 permits a year.
privacy_notes: The layer has OPERATOR, PRIOR_OPERATOR, DRILLER and MINERAL_OWNER, which can hold individuals or private landowners and the AGOL EDITOR and LAST_EDITED_USER columns hold staff user names; do not publish them without a corporate-name filter. Filed APDs carry contact names, phones and e-mails (not seen). Nothing was copied.
